title: Application segment wire behavior: what each SDK sends, drops and matches across the four segment kinds
aliases: browser access pra inspection segment update

prose.text: Core, Browser Access, Inspection and PRA segments share one endpoint, and the SDK models differ in what they send, drop and match on update. Field listings are in the generated surface layer; this subject holds only the behavior. {{variants-share-endpoint}}

prose.heading: Model tags that change the wire

prose.text: The `bypassOnReauth` tag differences are in [[zpa.app-segments.sdk-behavior]], the always-serialized parent flags in [[zpa.terraform.app-segment-lifecycle]], and the Go rule that a value struct tagged `omitempty` is still sent in [[shared.sdk-go.zero-value-writes]].

{{share-to-microtenants-tag}} {{share-to-microtenants-always-sent}} Whether the API treats that as removal is open {{gap:put-share-removal}}. Move and share bodies are in [[zpa.microtenants.share-and-move]]. {{move-share-return-204}}
{{application-type-validation}} {{delete-by-type-request}} What the delete removes is open {{gap:delete-by-type-scope}}.
{{application-summary-comment}} {{provision-python-only}} The weighted load balancer update that returns a nil object is in [[zpa.sdk-go.service-defects]].

checks.do: Whether an update from the Go SDK or Python SDK to a PRA, Inspection or Browser Access segment will drop or clear sub-applications, ports or flags, before blaming the API.
Whether the sub-application names or domains in the update match the existing ones, since Go matches by name and Python by domain.
Whether a call using an application type fails client-side in Go because the type is outside the three accepted values.
Whether the failing request sends `commonAppsDto: {}` or a null `zpnErId` that the variant's model always emits.

variants-share-endpoint.statement: The Go core, Browser Access, Inspection and PRA application segment packages all use the same `/application` endpoint under the customer path, and the API's create body takes the sub-application lists (`inspectionApps`, `praApps`, `clientlessApps`) and `commonAppsDto` in one schema whose `appsConfig` entries carry an `appTypes` list of BROWSER_ACCESS, SIPA, INSPECT or SECURE_REMOTE_ACCESS.
variants-share-endpoint.conditions: The specification shows one POST /application body schema and does not state how the server picks the segment kind; that the kind follows the presence of the sub-application arrays is the legacy reading and is not stated by any source.

subapp-read-write-fields.statement: The Go Inspection and PRA segment models read their sub-applications from `inspectionApps` and `praApps` respectively, and write them through `commonAppsDto.appsConfig`; the API create body defines `appsConfig` entries as CommonAppConfigDto.

common-apps-dto-always-emitted.statement: Both the Go Inspection and PRA segment models hold `CommonAppsDto` by value, the Inspection tag with `omitempty` and the PRA tag without it, so every create or update from either carries a `commonAppsDto` object, `{}` when no sub-applications are set. The Inspection tag does not make the object optional.
common-apps-dto-always-emitted.conditions: Applies the Go encoding/json rule recorded in the derived claim to these two fields. The Inspection Update also assigns an empty CommonAppsDto when there are no appsConfig entries (from v3.8.49, only when there are also no inspection apps to delete), which sends the same empty object.

segment-group-id-tags.statement: The Go PRA and core segment models send `segmentGroupId` without `omitempty` (an empty string goes on the wire), while the Inspection and Browser Access models tag it `omitempty`.

inspection-protection-flags-tags.statement: The Go Inspection model tags `adpEnabled` and `autoAppProtectEnabled` with `omitempty`, so an explicit false is not sent, while the core application segment model sends both without `omitempty`.

zpn-er-id-by-variant.statement: The Go PRA, Browser Access and core segment models carry `zpnErId` as a pointer without `omitempty`, so an unset value is sent as JSON null, and the Inspection model has no `zpnErId` field.

subapp-config-tags.statement: In the Go sub-application config, the Inspection entry sends `inspectAppId` and `enabled` without `omitempty` and tags `appId` `omitempty`, while the PRA entry sends `appId` and `praAppId` without `omitempty` and tags `enabled` `omitempty`, so an explicit false `enabled` on a PRA sub-application is not sent.

go-deleted-subapps.statement: The Go PRA `Update` computes `DeletedPraApps` from the existing PRA sub-applications whose IDs are not among the remaining `appsConfig` entries, and sends them. Before v3.8.49 the Go Inspection `Update` never set `DeletedInspectApps`, so a caller had to supply it to remove an Inspection sub-application; from v3.8.49 (#464) it computes `DeletedInspectApps` the same way, from the existing inspection apps whose IDs are not among the remaining `appsConfig` entries.

python-update-matches-by-domain.statement: The Python PRA, Inspection and Browser Access v2 segment updates fetch the existing sub-applications by type (SECURE_REMOTE_ACCESS, INSPECT, BROWSER_ACCESS), match each `apps_config` entry to them by domain, set the matched ID (or an empty string when the domain is new), and set `deleted_pra_apps`, `deleted_inspect_apps` or `deleted_ba_apps` to the existing sub-applications whose domain is no longer listed.

quotes: existing_apps = {s.domain: s for s in segments_list if s.app_id == segment_id}
if domain in existing_apps: app["pra_app_id"] = existing_apps[domain].id else: app["pra_app_id"] = ""
deleted_ids = [app.id for domain, app in existing_apps.items() if domain not in desired_domains]

python-update-matches-by-domain.conditions: The Go SDK matches Inspection and PRA sub-applications by name instead (zpa.terraform.app-segment-lifecycle:nested-apps-matched-by-name) and Browser Access by list position (zpa.terraform.app-segment-lifecycle:browser-child-id-positional-fallback). A sub-application whose domain changes is treated as new by the Python path.

python-inspection-update-ids.statement: The Python Inspection update sets `inspect_app_id` to the segment ID and then overwrites it with the matched existing sub-application ID or an empty string; it never assigns `app_id` on the `apps_config` entries, unlike the PRA and Browser Access v2 updates, which set `app_id` to the segment ID.

quotes: for app in common_apps_dto["apps_config"]: domain = app.get("domain") app["inspect_app_id"] = segment_id if domain in existing_apps: app["inspect_app_id"] = existing_apps[domain].id else: app["inspect_app_id"] = ""

python-inspection-update-ids.conditions: That app_id is never assigned in the Inspection update rests on reading the update function at the pin (the string app["app_id"] does not occur in app_segments_inspection.py). Whether the API needs appId on the entries when updating Inspection sub-applications is not established.

The Go variant updates tag the port lists omitempty, so an empty list is dropped there rather than sent. Restated to list all four port keys, since tcpPortRange is cleared in every variant too.

python-app-types-injection.statement: When an `apps_config` entry has no `app_types`, the Python PRA, Inspection and Browser Access v2 create and update functions set it to SECURE_REMOTE_ACCESS, INSPECT or BROWSER_ACCESS respectively before sending.
python-app-types-injection.conditions: The original app_segments_ba.py module contains no app_types handling (git grep app_types at the pin finds no match in it). Neither code path emits a warning when it injects the value.

share-to-microtenants-tag.statement: The Go core application segment model tags `shareToMicrotenants` without `omitempty`, while the neighbouring `clientlessApps` and `sharedMicrotenantDetails` tags carry it.
share-to-microtenants-tag.conditions: What the API does with a null or empty shareToMicrotenants on a segment PUT is open (gap put-share-removal); the dedicated share endpoint is recorded in zpa.microtenants.share-and-move.

share-to-microtenants-always-sent.statement: A create or update from that struct therefore always carries the shareToMicrotenants member: null for a nil slice, [] for an empty one.
share-to-microtenants-always-sent.conditions: Follows from Go encoding/json semantics (a field without omitempty is always marshalled; a nil slice encodes as null, an empty one as []). No captured source states this for this field. Split from share-to-microtenants-tag, whose Tier A statement keeps only the tag.

move-share-return-204.statement: The API documents No Content (204) as the success response of both the application segment move and share calls.

application-summary-comment.statement: The Go `GetApplicationSummary` carries the source comment 'Need to review as the API is returning 400 error' and reads the application summary path through `common.GetAllPagesGenericWithCustomFilters`, with a filter holding the service's microtenant ID.

provision-python-only.statement: The Python SDK has an `add_segment_provision` that posts to `/application/provision`, a path the OpenAPI document does not define.
provision-python-only.conditions: No path with `/provision` appears among the Go ZPA service packages for application segments: `git grep -n /provision HEAD -- zscaler/zpa` in the Go SDK matched only provisioning-key URLs. Absence in the Go SDK is not evidence that the endpoint does not exist.

delete-by-type-request.statement: Deleting a sub-application by type is `DELETE /application/{id}/deleteAppByType` with the application type as a query parameter; the Go function sends only the type and the Microtenant filter, while Go's other segment deletes pass `ForceDelete: true`, and the Python function sends `applicationType` and an optional `microtenantId`.

params = {"applicationType": application_type} if microtenant_id: params["microtenantId"] = microtenant_id request, error = self._request_executor.create_request(http_method, api_url, params=params)

delete-by-type-request.conditions: Whether the endpoint accepts forceDelete, and what it removes, is open (gap delete-by-type-scope).

application-type-validation.statement: The Go `GetByApplicationType` and `DeleteByApplicationType` reject any application type other than BROWSER_ACCESS, INSPECT or SECURE_REMOTE_ACCESS before sending a request, while the Python `get_segments_by_type` only requires a non-empty type and `delete_segments_by_type` does not check it; the API documents `applicationType` as a required string without an enum.

application-type-validation.conditions: Corrects the legacy statement that both SDKs validate the set client-side: the Python docstrings list the three values but no code compares them.

connection-security-values.statement: The API's `connectionSecurity` on a PRA sub-application takes ANY, NLA, NLA_EXT, TLS, VM_CONNECT or RDP, and the Python docstring lists the same six; the Go PRA sub-application field is a plain string with no value list.
connection-security-values.conditions: Settles the legacy open question that NLA was unconfirmed (ledger zpa-24): the API specification lists it. Corrects the legacy statement that the Go struct agrees with a five-value list. A schema enum is not a live acceptance test.

bulk-multimatch-id-type.summary: The Go bulk Multimatch update types the application IDs as integers, while the Python SDK documents and exemplifies string IDs and passes the body through unchanged.

positions.says: The Go payload serializes `applicationIds` as JSON numbers.
The Python docstring takes a list of string IDs and sends the keyword arguments as the body.

quotes: application_ids (list of str): List of application segment IDs to update.

bulk-multimatch-id-type.impact: The two SDKs send different JSON types to the same PUT /application/bulkUpdateMultiMatch. The OpenAPI document does not define the endpoint, so no source says which form the API accepts; a call that fails with one SDK may need the other form.

put-share-removal.title: Whether a segment PUT carrying a null or empty shareToMicrotenants removes existing shares
put-share-removal.blocks: telling whether the always-sent shareToMicrotenants member in the Go core model can unshare a segment on an unrelated update
put-share-removal.detail: Unverified legacy statement: an empty slice serializes and can trigger removal of existing shares on an inadvertent PUT. No source states the server behavior. In a scratch tenant, share a segment, PUT the segment with shareToMicrotenants omitted, null and [], and read the sharing state after each.

delete-by-type-scope.title: What DELETE deleteAppByType removes and whether it accepts forceDelete
delete-by-type-scope.blocks: telling whether deleting a typed sub-application leaves the parent segment and whether a force flag has any effect
delete-by-type-scope.detail: Unverified legacy statement: this endpoint does not accept forceDelete and deletes only the typed child record, not the parent application segment. The SDK code only shows the applicationType query parameter; the OpenAPI document does not define the path.
